title: Choose a workflow before choosing a tool
lead: Personal notes, team discussions, and long-term archiving need not start with the same workflow.
intro: Imagine a small team organizing research material. Some people want to revise freely, others need to discuss it together, and others only need the final conclusions. This fictional scenario demonstrates a comparison table, not a particular software product.

sections.title: I. Put different needs in one table

table.caption: An illustrative decision framework: compare approaches, not product scores
rows: Personal, ongoing organization with a self-managed file structure
A team discussing frequently updated material
Access permissions, collaboration agreements, and offline copies
Turn material into readable conclusions for an audience
Save the edited file; this is not a live collaboration system

sections.title: II. Explain what the table leaves out

items.title: Start with the reader
items.lead: Know the audience before deciding how much detail to include.
paragraphs: Readers making a decision can start with a conditional conclusion and a comparison table. Readers tracing the evidence need clear sources and limitations.

items.title: Then consider delivery
items.lead: Editable and portable does not mean every format has a direct export button.
bullets: The current template supports direct editing and saving as HTML.
PDF uses browser printing; there is no Markdown export button yet.

conclusion.title: Put needs before tools
paragraphs: Describe the use case and limitations before choosing an approach. This example demonstrates report structure, not a product review or purchasing recommendation.

footerNote: Fictional scenario showing comparison tables, categorized entries, and conclusions. Generated by this repository; not a Dia product screenshot.
